content.user_title: Instrument Azure apps with Application Insights
content.value_statement: Adding reliable telemetry to Azure-hosted apps can be hard across frameworks and deployment models. This skill provides concise Application Insights setup guidance, SDK references, and Azure configuration patterns.
actual_capabilities: Explain when to use auto-instrumentation for Azure App Service apps.
Provide Bicep guidance for Application Insights and Log Analytics resources.
Give ASP.NET Core, Node.js, and Python SDK setup steps.
Show how to configure APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING in Azure-hosted apps.
Summarize Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry references for Python, TypeScript, and Java.
limitations: It provides guidance and does not safely orchestrate project changes by itself.
It assumes Azure hosting and is most specific for Azure App Service scenarios.
It does not validate Azure subscription permissions or live resource state.
It does not replace official documentation for version-specific SDK changes.

prompt_templates.title: Find the right setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to identify the best Application Insights instrumentation path for my Azure-hosted web app. Ask me for any missing language, framework, and hosting details.

prompt_templates.title: Plan ASP.NET Core telemetry
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the Application Insights setup for an ASP.NET Core app on Azure App Service. Include package, code, and environment configuration steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Node.js readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review a Node.js Azure app for Application Insights instrumentation. List the entry point, environment variable needs, and deployment notes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare deployment options
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to compare auto-instrumentation, Bicep resource creation, and SDK-based instrumentation for my Azure web workload. Include tradeoffs and prerequisites.

output_examples.input: I have an ASP.NET Core app running in Azure App Service.
output_examples.output: Recommended path: use Azure App Service auto-instrumentation first if your runtime is supported. For code-level telemetry, add the Azure Monitor package and initialize OpenTelemetry before app build. Store the connection string in Azure app settings.

output_examples.input: We use Node.js and need Application Insights guidance.
output_examples.output: Recommended path: add the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry package, initialize it near the start of the entry file, and load the Application Insights connection string before telemetry setup begins.

output_examples.input: Our team provisions Azure resources with Bicep.
output_examples.output: Recommended path: add Application Insights and a Log Analytics workspace to the infrastructure template. Then expose the connection string through the hosted app configuration.

best_practices: Confirm language, framework, and hosting before choosing an instrumentation path.
Store the connection string in Azure app settings or IaC, not in source files.
Prefer auto-instrumentation only when the hosting platform and language support it.
anti_patterns: Using this skill to make project edits when an orchestration skill should handle changes.
Placing the Application Insights connection string in appsettings.json or committed files.
Initializing Node.js telemetry after application modules are already loaded.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my application?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and reference material for planning Application Insights instrumentation.

faq.question: Which application types does it cover best?
faq.answer: It covers ASP.NET Core, Node.js, and Python web applications hosted in Azure.

faq.question: Can it help with auto-instrumentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains when Azure App Service auto-instrumentation may be a good fit.

faq.question: Does it include infrastructure guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a Bicep example for Application Insights with Log Analytics.

faq.question: How should connection strings be handled?
faq.answer: Use Azure app settings or infrastructure templates. Do not commit connection strings to source files.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude?
faq.answer: No. It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
